step1_analysis.description: This circuit appears to be an operational amplifier or error amplifier used within the delta-sigma control loop of the switched-capacitor voltage regulator. It features multiple input/bias branches and MOS capacitors for compensation or filtering.

paper_reference.title: Noise-Shaping Techniques Applied to Switched-Capacitor Voltage Regulators

dc_power.description: Total DC power consumption of the circuit

sky130_expected.calculation: Sum of currents from VDD and VOUT multiplied by their respective voltages.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical bias currents for error amplifiers in regulators are in the tens of microamps.
Single or two-stage amplifiers in 1.8V SKY130 typically achieve 20-60 dB open-loop gain depending on the load and cascoding.

sky130_expected.calculation: Frequency where AC gain crosses 0 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: To support a 1 MHz clock, the amplifier bandwidth should be at least 5-10 times higher to settle within half a clock period.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC operating point, power consumption, and AC frequency response of the amplifier.

* Voltage Sources
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVOUT VOUT 0 1.8

* Biasing and Inputs
VLABEL_NET_0 LABEL_NET_0 0 0.9 ac 1

VLABEL_NET_20 LABEL_NET_20 0 0.9

* Load Capacitor
CLOAD N6 0 100f

.control
* DC Operating Point
op
let dc_power = (-i(VVDD) - i(VVOUT)) * 1.8
print dc_power

* AC Analysis
ac dec 100 1k 1G
let gain_db = vdb(N6)
meas ac low_freq_gain find gain_db at=1k
meas ac unity_gain_bw when gain_db=0 fall=1

* Transient Analysis
tran 1n 2u
meas tran v_out_max max v(N6)
meas tran v_out_min min v(N6)

quit
.endc
